**Continuous 2.26.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.26.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.26.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.26.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.26.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.26.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.26.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.26.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.26.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.26.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.26.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.26.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.24.0

This release is about finding and keeping your sessions, and about long-running commands. The terminal agent's `--resume` and session picker and the IDE's History page group sessions by folder, with the newest session of this folder first, and `--resume` no longer continues another project's conversation. A deleted session goes to a trash for 7 days, History search reads message text, and an unsent message survives a reload. Provider connections have their own Settings page. Terminal commands can no longer flood the window: their output is bounded, runaways are stopped, and the full output is kept in a file the model can search. It also fixes a Bedrock error that broke every request after a reply was stopped while Claude was thinking.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### New

- **Command output is bounded, and runaway commands are stopped.** The agent's terminal commands keep the first 64 KB and the last 1 MiB of output in memory. The model gets the whole output when it fits; otherwise a note, the first and last parts of 30,000 characters (10,000 for a failed command) and the path of the full output, which is written to `~/.continuous/command-output/` once it is long (at most 512 MiB, which stops the command; files older than 7 days are deleted). The terminal card updates at most every 100 ms with the last 400 lines, a size meter and **Open full output**. A command that prints more than 1 MB/s for 10 seconds, 100 MB in all, or the same line or block over and over is stopped with its process tree, and the model is told why; at Tools = Permissive or IDGAF it keeps running and writes to its file. Two new tools: `read_command_output` (the end of a command's output, or the lines matching a pattern, with line numbers) and `stop_command`.
- `continuous --resume <sessionId>` resumes that session. `continuous ls` and the `--resume` picker group sessions by folder: this folder first with its newest session selected, then the other folders, then sessions without a folder. `ls --json` adds `inWorkspace` and `workspaceGroup`.
- The IDE History page groups sessions by workspace folder, the open workspace first and expanded; **Group by: Date** keeps the old view.
- Deleted sessions go to a trash for 7 days (`~/.continuous/sessions-trash/`). The History page shows **Undo** after a delete and a **Trash** group with **Restore** and **Delete permanently**; the terminal agent has `continuous sessions trash` and `continuous sessions restore <id>`. A session open in another window or agent is moved only after you confirm.
- The History search box also finds words in message text, not only titles: titles still match as you type, and a moment later sessions whose messages hold every word are added with the matching text shown. It reads the 200 most recently written sessions and says when it stopped early.
- The terminal session picker (`continuous ls`, `--resume`, `/resume`) filters as you type (title, first message, folder). Del, then `y`, moves the selected session to the trash; Ctrl+U puts it back.
- In the IDE, an unsent message is kept per session: the chat input and an edit of an earlier message that is in progress come back after a window reload, an extension update or a crash, with a notice. @-mention chips come back as chips; a pasted image is not kept and the notice says so. Sending clears it, and opening another session shows that session's draft.
- Command Palette: **Open Permissions**, **Open the Audit Inbox**, **Open Stats**, **Stop Response**, **Resume Response**, **Start Loop**, **Stop Loop**, **Show Agents** and **Test Connection of the Chat Model**, each doing what its control in the panel does. None has a default key.
- Model retirement warnings in the IDE beyond the input-toolbar chip: the model picker marks a configured model that is deprecated, retired or retiring soon (for example "(retires 2026-11-30)", with the full sentence and the suggested successor in the tooltip), Settings > Models states it under the role that uses the model, and loading a config warns once per model. Sources: Anthropic's deprecations page (checked-in table, read 2026-11-11; first-party Anthropic only, never Bedrock or Vertex) and the `deprecated` / `retiresAt` fields of a model list you fetched in Add model. Anthropic retires `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` on 2026-11-30 (successor `claude-sonnet-5-5`) and `claude-opus-4-5-20251101` not before 2026-11-24 (suggested `claude-opus-5-5`).
- **Settings > Providers**: a page of its own for provider connections, beside Models, so they no longer sit behind Add model. Each connection shows its provider, account or endpoint and region, how it signs in (key in secure storage or `~/.continuous/.env`, environment variable, AWS profile or default credentials; never the key) and how many models are enabled, with **Manage models**, **Edit connection**, **Test connection** and **Remove** (which says what leaves `config.yaml` and that stored keys stay). Provider accounts moved there from Settings > Models. Reach it from the Settings sidebar, **Providers...** on Settings > Models and in the model picker, or the Command Palette's **Open Providers** (no default key).
- `continuous acp` lists and reopens earlier sessions: `session/list` (filtered by the editor's folder, paged), `session/load`, which replays the conversation and its tool calls, and `session/resume`. It now advertises `loadSession`. Sessions saved by the terminal agent and by the IDE both open. The protocol version stays 1.

### Behaviour changes

- Delete on the History page and in the terminal picker no longer removes a session at once: it can be restored for 7 days. **Clear chats** still deletes everything, the trash included.
- In the terminal session picker, letters type into the filter, so `j` and `k` no longer move the selection; use the arrow keys (or Ctrl+N and Ctrl+P). Esc clears the filter, and leaves when it is empty.
- `continuous --resume` in a terminal opens the session picker with the newest session of this folder selected (Enter resumes it) instead of resuming the newest session of any folder. Headless `-p --resume` resumes the newest session of this folder (a subfolder, a parent folder or the same git repository counts); when there is none it resumes the newest overall and says which folder it came from.
- Add model > Anthropic no longer offers Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.5 (both retiring; Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5 stay at the top of the list) or the retired Claude Opus 4.1 and Claude Sonnet 4. A new config created from the assistant template uses `claude-sonnet-5-5` instead of the retired `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`. Existing configs and pricing for the old ids are unchanged.

### Removed

- The **Enter Enterprise License Key** command, an upstream leftover: nothing in Continuous answers its request, so it called every key invalid. The second palette entry for `continuous.focusContinuousInput` ("Focus Continuous Chat") is gone too; the command stays as **Add Highlighted Code to Context and Clear Chat**.

### Fixes

- **Bedrock: "thinking.signature: Field required".** A Claude thinking block without a signature, left by a reply stopped or cut off while thinking, or by reasoning from a model that does not sign it (GPT OSS, Kimi) before a switch to Claude, is now left out of the request. Before, Claude refused the request, and every later request in the session failed. Other model families get their reasoning back as before.
- **Context overflow from vLLM.** Bedrock GPT OSS words an over-long prompt as "Input length (…) exceeds model's maximum context length (…)"; it is now read with both sizes, so the chat shows the overflow panel with **Try again** and **New session** and corrects its context estimate for that model, instead of the raw error.
- **Stop ends the whole command.** Stopping a terminal command ends its process tree, on Windows too, where only the shell was ended; every command the agent started is ended when the window closes. A command run with `waitForCompletion: false` no longer rewrites a message already sent, which broke the prompt cache.
- The History page's row actions (Edit, Save as Markdown, Archive, Delete) can be reached with the keyboard: Tab to a row (Enter opens it, Delete deletes it) and Tab again to its buttons, which show on hover and while the row has focus. Before, they were only in the page while the mouse was over the row.
- `--resume` no longer continues another project's conversation, and a session picked in `continuous ls` is the one resumed (it could resume the newest session instead).
- In the IDE, **Last Session** and the session restored when a window starts come from the open workspace. Windows share the stored last session, so a window could open another workspace's conversation.

### Upgrade notes

- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** No new host.
- **New folders in `~/.continuous`.** `sessions-trash/` (deleted sessions, purged after 7 days) and `command-output/` (the full output of long agent commands, raw and unmasked, deleted after 7 days; delete it at any time).
- **Picking a session.** In the terminal, `continuous --resume` now opens the picker instead of resuming at once; Enter resumes the newest session of this folder. Scripts should use `-p --resume` or `--resume <sessionId>`.
- **Delete is undoable.** Deleting a session moves it to the trash; **Empty trash**, or `continuous sessions trash --empty --yes`, frees the space at once.
